speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I'm Dr. Agent. To help narrow down the cause of your pruritic rash, can you describe the appearance of the lesions in detail, such as whether they are raised, flat, or fluid-filled? Also, have you traveled recently or started any new medications in the last two weeks?

speaker: Patient
text: 11-year-old girl. The patient has been experiencing a mildly pruritic rash on her trunk and extremities for 2 days. One week ago, she developed symptoms of low-grade fever, rhinorrhea, and headache. A facial rash appeared 4 days later, sparing the perioral area.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for that information. Does the rash on her trunk and extremities consist of small red spots that look like they have a "dewdrop on a rose petal" appearance? Also, has she been in close contact with anyone else who has had chickenpox or a similar rash recently?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Mildly pruritic rash on trunk and extremities. I also have Low-grade fever, Rhinorrhea, Headache, Facial rash not involving the perioral skin.

speaker: Doctor
text: The description of a facial rash sparing the perioral area, followed by a trunk and extremity rash, is highly characteristic of Erythema Infectiosum, also known as Fifth Disease. To confirm this, has she had any joint pain, and does the rash on her body appear lacy or reticular?

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: No significant past medical history. Social history: Attends local school. Lives with parents and one younger sibling. No recent travel history.

speaker: Doctor
text:
The clinical presentation of a facial rash sparing the perioral area followed by a lacy, pruritic rash on the trunk and extremities is classic for Parvovirus B19 infection. I will proceed with the diagnosis based on these characteristic findings.

DIAGNOSIS READY: Erythema Infectiosum (Fifth Disease)
